summary: Music no longer goes permanently silent after an unheard track: the audio controller's no-overlap barrier could be poisoned by a kill that never reported back, and every later play was then deferred forever.
details: Root cause, measured 2026-09-22: an AutoPaused AudioPlayer never drains the audio resource, so a killed ffmpeg's piped stdout stays back-pressured and Node never emits 'close' for it (PIPED-unread: exited=true, closed=false, 64KiB buffered; the same kill with no pipeline closes normally). The close promise never settled, the reap barrier never emptied, and every subsequent play was deferred on a barrier that could no longer be crossed — no ffmpeg process, no log line, no event, until the process was restarted. It explains the 2026-09-21 outage exactly: two accepted plays, no ffmpeg in the container, and 25 hours of uptime.

Every hard cut now stops the player with force. `stop(false)` on an AutoPaused player returns early without leaving AutoPause (@discordjs/voice 0.19.2), so it could never release the pipeline; force reaches Idle, which destroys the play stream and lets the reap complete.
`killProc` also destroys the child's stdout and stderr, so a reap can complete regardless of any @discordjs/voice behaviour.

The barrier itself is now bounded. Past the SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL escalation there is no live process left to overlap, so a spawn is no longer allowed to wait on it forever; a barrier that times out is logged and cleared.

`pending_reaps` is reported in /voice/status, and a deferred spawn is logged. A non-zero count while nothing is playing is the wedge, provable in one request, where before it could only be inferred from missing log lines.

Three corrections to the previous release's start deadline: a track suspended by speech is now held to a deadline too (only an arriving play was, so a track that was already playing could still be stranded), reviving a suspended track no longer leaves the parked slot's timer armed, and a play waiting behind speech gets a much longer deadline than a spawn so a full speech queue cannot kill it spuriously.
limitations: The mechanism is confirmed by measurement, but its attribution to the 2026-09-21 outage remains inferential: the poisoning kill happened before the surviving log window, and those container logs were destroyed by the restart that restored service. The new `pending_reaps` read-back is what would settle it on a recurrence.
This does not address nora's own side, which still treats a playback id as proof that audio is flowing, never reads the controller's player status, and never polls it.
